title: 마음을 말해요: 서운하다, 부럽다, 답답하다
objective: By the end, you can choose the right word for 10 subtle feelings (서운하다, 부럽다, 답답하다, 걱정되다, 억울하다 and more) and use it in a short sentence about something that happened.
summary: Ten everyday Korean words for subtle feelings, such as feeling hurt, jealous, frustrated or treated unfairly, each with a short real-life example.

task.title: Choose and use feelings
task.line: Read each situation, decide how the person feels, and choose or write the right feeling word in the form shown.

words.meaning: to feel hurt or let down (by someone close to you)
words.example: 친구가 제 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 서운했어요.
words.exampleMeaning: I felt a little hurt because my friend forgot my birthday.

words.meaning: to be jealous, to wish you had what someone else has
words.example: 다음 주에 제주도 가요? 와, 정말 부러워요!
words.exampleMeaning: You're going to Jeju next week? Wow, I'm so jealous!

words.meaning: to feel frustrated because things don't go well or you can't express yourself
words.example: 하고 싶은 말이 있는데 한국어로 못 하니까 답답해요.
words.exampleMeaning: I have something to say but can't say it in Korean, so I feel frustrated.

words.meaning: to feel it is unfair, to be blamed for something you didn't do
words.example: 제가 안 깼는데 왜 저한테 화를 내요? 억울해요.
words.exampleMeaning: I didn't break it, so why are you angry at me? It's not fair.

words.meaning: to feel it's a pity, to wish something had happened
words.example: 시간이 없어서 그 카페에 못 가 본 게 아쉬워요.
words.exampleMeaning: It's a pity I didn't have time to go to that cafe.

words.meaning: to be upset and sad about a bad result
words.exampleMeaning: I'm upset because I studied hard but failed the exam.

words.meaning: to feel embarrassed in front of other people
words.exampleMeaning: I fell in front of people, so I was really embarrassed.

words.meaning: to be disappointed when something is not as good as you expected
words.exampleMeaning: I expected a lot, but the movie wasn't great, so I was disappointed.

words.meaning: to be flustered, not knowing what to do in a sudden situation
words.exampleMeaning: I was about to pay but didn't have my wallet, so I panicked.

exercises: Choose the right word: ① 친구는 매일 맛있는 것을 먹으러 다녀요. 저는 그 친구가 (부러워요 / 억울해요). ② 동생이 컵을 깼는데 엄마가 저한테 화를 내셨어요. 정말 (서운했어요 / 억울했어요). ③ 길이 너무 막혀서 버스가 10분째 안 움직여요. 정말 (답답해요 / 창피해요).
Use each word once (창피하다, 걱정되다, 실망하다) and write the dictionary form: ① 회의 시간에 제 휴대폰 벨 소리가 크게 울렸어요. 모두 저를 봤어요. ② 밤 11시인데 아이가 아직 집에 안 왔어요. ③ 몇 달 동안 기다린 콘서트가 생각보다 재미없었어요.
Write the word in brackets in the past form (-았어요/었어요/했어요): ① 갑자기 선생님이 제 이름을 불러서 ____. (당황하다) ② 비가 와서 소풍을 못 갔어요. 정말 ____. (아쉽다) ③ 새로 산 우산을 지하철에 두고 내려서 ____. (속상하다)
Complete the dialogue with 답답하다, 서운하다 or 부럽다 in the -아요/어요 form: ① A: 왜 한숨을 쉬어요? B: 컴퓨터가 너무 느려서 ____. ② A: 표정이 안 좋아요. B: 제일 친한 친구가 저만 빼고 놀러 갔어요. 좀 ____. ③ A: 민수 씨 남편은 요리를 정말 잘한대요. B: 와, ____!
Answer the question in Korean with one full sentence using -아서/어서 and 억울했어요: 언제 억울했어요?
answers: ① 부러워요 ② 억울했어요 ③ 답답해요
① 창피하다 ② 걱정되다 ③ 실망하다
① 당황했어요 ② 아쉬웠어요 ③ 속상했어요
① 답답해요 ② 서운해요 ③ 부러워요
(Sample answer) 제가 안 늦었는데 늦었다고 혼나서 억울했어요.
